title: I'm going to explain it in very simple terms
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What do you do when a book, or a deal, moves faster than your vocabulary?

Jose said this is a really dense chapter. We really have to prepare to even begin to discuss it. He goes very, very fast, and there is a lot more background to what he is doing than the narrative of the book.
If you don't understand the language, he said, it gets more complicated and you feel a little lost. So it is a good opportunity to learn the language and the business concepts of what he is doing.
A student agreed: there was a lot going on, some terms, and I was confused about the networks and who they belong to.

Jose gave a list of words to look up: antitrust, the difference between a broadcast network and a cable network, what a news bureau is, the big three networks, what an IPO is when a company goes public, and what a reverse merger is.
He suggested searching the company's timeline on an encyclopedia site, so you can see the progression of the acquisitions.

groups.heading: I had no idea what was happening

lines.text: I was a literature teacher, Jose said. I was not a business professor. But in my twenties, at twenty-five or twenty-six, I was the founder of a company that went public on the Nasdaq.

I had no idea what was happening, honestly, he said. I had a lot of older people around me who tried to explain it to me. So I went through a learning curve, as you are going through now with me in this book.
It is beautiful that we are reading the story, he said, and at the same time getting all this mechanical business knowledge. As entrepreneurs you will be able to talk about these terms with fluency.
Which word on that list do you not yet understand?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the business words you hear and do not fully understand.
Pick two and look them up.
Write each one in a sentence of your own.
Write one thing in your own work where this word matters.
Write who you could ask to explain it.

check.q: What did Jose say you feel if you don't understand the language?
What did Jose say he was in his twenties?
choices: The founder of a company that went public on the Nasdaq

check.q: What did Jose say about the older people who explained things to him?
choices: They tried to explain it, and he went through a learning curve
They did it all for him

recap: Learn the language of business. Everyone goes through a learning curve.
